topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the lecture series, and the key learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogens, methodologies, and cancer initiation and promotion.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetic Basis, Random Chance, and Epidemiological Variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental mechanisms of cancer development and debate the relative contributions of intrinsic biological bad luck versus environmental exposures using global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious and Chemical Carcinogens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific biological agents, dietary toxins, radiation, and chemical exposures induce DNA damage and mutations through direct reactivity or xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic factors like chronic inflammation, tumor-promoting chemical agonists, and host developmental timing provide the permissive environment for mutated cells to progress into cancer.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate genomic mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo animal studies, and in vitro assays used to identify and validate carcinogenic agents.
